from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            "Vectors i and j define a square.",
            "The square deforms into a parallelogram."
        ])

        # Assets paths
        grid_asset = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg"

        vector_asset = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vector.svg"
        parallelogram_asset = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/parallelogram.svg"

        # Load SVG assets
        grid_svg = SVGMobject(grid_asset).set_color(WHITE)
        origin_svg = SVGMobject(origin_asset).set_color("#FF0000")
        i_vec_svg = SVGMobject(vector_asset).set_color("#00FF00")
        j_vec_svg = SVGMobject(vector_asset).set_color("#0000FF")
        para_svg = SVGMobject(parallelogram_asset).set_color(WHITE).set_fill(opacity=0.2)

        # Place grid
        self.place_in_area(grid_svg, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        # Origin and vectors
        self.place_at_grid(origin_svg, 'D3', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(i_vec_svg, 'D4', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(j_vec_svg, 'C3', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(origin_svg), FadeIn(i_vec_svg), FadeIn(j_vec_svg))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        # Square definition
        square = Square(side_length=1, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'D3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(square))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        # Transform into parallelogram
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(square, para_svg),
            i_vec_svg.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.5 + UP * 0.5),
            j_vec_svg.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.5)
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Negative determinant means a flip.", "Zero determinant squashes the plane.", "Dimension is lost at zero."]
        self.setup_layout("The Meaning of Sign and Zero", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visual elements
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        # B3 is roughly in the middle-right
        self.place_at_grid(square, "B3", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Negative determinant means a flip.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Flip visual: reflection
        reflection = square.copy().set_color(RED).flip(axis=UP)
        self.play(Transform(square, reflection), run_time=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Zero determinant squashes the plane.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        # Squashing: flatten to line
        line = Line(start=LEFT*1, end=RIGHT*1, color="#FF00FF", stroke_width=6)
        self.place_at_grid(line, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(square.animate.stretch(0, 0), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Dimension is lost at zero.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        lost_label = Text("Lost Dimension", color=RED, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(lost_label, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(lost_label), Indicate(line))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Use formula det equals ad minus bc.",
            "Connects formula to geometric side lengths.",
            "Example shows unit square becomes rectangle."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Calculation Method (The 2x2 Case)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define matrix
        mat = MathTex(r"\det\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} = ad - bc", font_size=40)
        self.place_at_grid(mat, "B3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(mat))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        ad_part = MathTex("ad", color="#00FF00")
        bc_part = MathTex("bc", color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(ad_part, "D2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(bc_part, "D4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(ad_part), FadeIn(bc_part))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        result = MathTex(r"ad - bc", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(result, "E3", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(ad_part, result), TransformFromCopy(bc_part, result))
        self.play(FadeIn(result))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Application", [
            "Determinant is a core diagnostic tool.",
            "Non-zero means a unique solution.",
            "Zero means the system is singular."
        ])

        # Objects
        square = Square(side_length=2, color=BLUE)
        det_label = MathTex(r"\det(A) = k", font_size=36)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1: Determinant is a core diagnostic tool ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'C2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(square))
        self.place_at_grid(det_label, 'C5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(det_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2: Non-zero means a unique solution ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(square.animate.scale(1.5), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Indicate(det_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3: Zero means the system is singular ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.play(square.animate.scale(0.01), FadeOut(square), run_time=1.5)
        zero_label = Text("Singular! Determinant = 0", color=RED, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(zero_label, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(zero_label))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Understanding the Determinant: The Geometry of Scaling

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Linear Transformation
sections.content: Briefly introduce vectors and how a 2x2 matrix transforms the 2D plane. Visual focus: A unit square (defined by vectors i and j) being stretched or sheared into a parallelogram.
sections.example: Visualize a robotic arm moving from point (1,0) to (2,1); the matrix captures how the underlying grid deforms.

sections.title: Defining the Determinant
sections.content: Define the determinant as the 'area scaling factor' of the transformation. If the transformation maps a shape to a region, the determinant is how many times the original area has expanded or shrunk.
sections.example: If a 1x1 square transforms into a parallelogram with an area of 5, the determinant of the transformation matrix is 5.

sections.title: The Meaning of Sign and Zero
sections.content: Explain that a negative determinant means the transformation involves a 'flip' (reflection). A zero determinant means the transformation squashes the plane into a line or point, losing a dimension.
sections.example: Think of a 'magic mirror'—a positive determinant is a clear image, a negative one is a reflection, and a zero determinant is like squashing a 3D cat into a 2D flat paper cutout.

sections.title: Calculation Method (The 2x2 Case)
sections.content: Introduce the standard formula det([[a, b], [c, d]]) = ad - bc. Connect the formula back to the visual geometry of the parallelogram side lengths.
sections.example: Calculate the determinant of matrix [[3, 1], [0, 2]]. Show the visual result: the unit square becomes a rectangle with base 3 and height 2, area = 6.

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
sections.content: Summarize that the determinant is a core diagnostic tool for matrices—telling us if a system has a unique solution (non-zero) or is singular (zero).
sections.example: In computer graphics, if your determinant is 0, your 3D model has collapsed into a flat shape—your code has a bug!
